The museum has a beautiful red sphalerite crystal.
Subjectivism says that truth depends on each person's mind.
Subjectivism says beauty is only in the eye of the beholder.
The philosophy class debated subjectivism for an hour.
Critics say subjectivism makes all opinions equal.
A thuja is an evergreen tree often used for hedges.
We planted a row of thuja along the fence.
Thuja hedges stay green all winter.
Water the young thuja often in summer.
Tuberculin is used in a skin test for tuberculosis.
The nurse injected a little tuberculin into my arm.
Come back in two days to check the tuberculin test.
Some jobs require a tuberculin test before you start.
An eponym is a word named after a person.
"Sandwich" is an eponym from an English earl.
Many diseases are eponyms named after doctors.
The teacher asked us to find five eponyms in English.
A chelate is a compound where a metal is held by a molecule.
Iron chelate helps plants with yellow leaves.
This garden fertilizer contains zinc chelate for healthy plants.
Doctors use chelates to remove lead from the body.
Aitch is the name of the letter H.
How do you spell it? With an aitch at the start.
Some people drop the aitch in words like "house."
Write a capital aitch on the board.
A gourami is a small, colorful fish for home aquariums.
We bought two blue gouramis for our fish tank.
Gouramis come up to the surface to breathe air.
The pet shop says gouramis are easy to keep.
A fumigant is a gas used to kill pests.
The company used a fumigant to kill termites in the house.
Leave the building while the fumigant is working.
Farmers use fumigants to protect stored grain.
A hadrosaur was a dinosaur with a flat, duck-like mouth.
Hadrosaurs ate plants and lived in large groups.
Scientists found hadrosaur eggs in the desert.
The kids saw a hadrosaur skeleton at the museum.
The boliviano is the money used in Bolivia.
A taxi ride costs about twenty bolivianos.
Change your dollars into bolivianos at the airport.
The hotel price is three hundred bolivianos a night.
A classicist studies ancient Greek and Roman culture.
My professor is a classicist who reads Latin every day.
The classicist translated the old poem into English.
Classicists study old texts and ancient art.
An extremophile is a living thing that survives extreme conditions.
Some extremophiles live in boiling hot springs.
Scientists study extremophiles to search for life on other planets.
Tiny tardigrades are famous extremophiles that survive almost anything.
An anabasis is a military march inland from the coast.
Xenophon wrote about the anabasis of the Greek army.
The anabasis took the soldiers deep into Persia.
We read part of the Anabasis in our history class.
A canonist is an expert in church law.
The bishop asked a canonist for advice.
The canonist explained the rules of marriage in the church.
He studied for years to become a canonist.
An epicycle is a small circle that moves along a bigger circle.
Old astronomers used epicycles to explain planet movements.
Ptolemy added epicycles to his model of the sky.
The epicycle idea was dropped after Kepler.
A polaron is an electron moving with a distortion in a crystal.
The physicist studies polarons in new solar materials.
Polarons can slow down electricity in some materials.
The paper describes how polarons move in the crystal.
A tropism is a plant's growth toward or away from something.
Growing toward the sun is a tropism.
Roots show a tropism toward water.
We did an experiment on tropism with bean plants.
The loti is the money used in Lesotho.
The bus ticket cost ten loti.
You can also pay with South African money instead of loti.
I changed some dollars into loti at the border.
loti.note: "Loti" is plural too; the singular is also "loti" (plural "maloti").

ex: A crystallite is a tiny crystal inside a solid material.
Metals are made of many small crystallites.
The scientist measured the size of each crystallite.
Smaller crystallites can make a metal stronger.
A kelpie is a water spirit in Scottish stories that looks like a horse.
The kelpie pulled people into the lake.
Children were told stories about the kelpie to keep them away from water.
In the old tale, a kelpie appears as a black horse.
A subproject is a smaller part of a bigger project.
Each team leads its own subproject.
The first subproject must finish by June.
We split the work into three subprojects.
A kimura is an arm lock used in grappling sports.
He won the match with a kimura in the second round.
Our coach showed us how to do a kimura safely.
Tap out quickly if someone puts you in a kimura.
Avifauna means all the birds that live in an area.
The island's avifauna includes many rare species.
Scientists counted the avifauna of the wetland.
The new road may harm the local avifauna.
A cyanate is a chemical containing carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen.
Potassium cyanate is used to make some medicines.
Cyanate is much less toxic than cyanide.
Urea can slowly break down into cyanate.
A deflator is a number used to remove the effect of rising prices.
Economists use the GDP deflator to measure real growth.
The deflator rose by three percent last year.
Divide the price by the deflator to compare years.
Dysthymia is a long-lasting, mild form of depression.
He has had dysthymia for many years.
Dysthymia can make you feel low most days.
Therapy can help people with dysthymia.
A galvanometer measures small electric currents.
The galvanometer needle moved when we closed the circuit.
Our physics lab has an old galvanometer.
Connect the wires to the galvanometer and watch the needle.
Gangsterism means violent crime by organized gangs.
The city is trying to fight gangsterism in its poorest areas.
Gangsterism grew during the years of prohibition.
The mayor promised to end gangsterism in the neighborhood.
Mandragora is another name for the mandrake plant.
People once thought mandragora had magic powers.
The roots of mandragora can look like a small person.
Mandragora is poisonous, so do not eat it.
Pregabalin is a medicine for nerve pain.
The doctor prescribed pregabalin for my back pain.
Pregabalin can make you feel dizzy at first.
Do not drink alcohol while taking pregabalin.
Rhodamine is a bright pink dye that glows.
Scientists use rhodamine to follow water in rivers.
The rhodamine glowed under the green light.
A little rhodamine colored the whole tank pink.
Rickettsia is a germ spread by ticks and lice.
A tick bite gave him a rickettsia infection.
Rickettsia can cause fever and a rash.
Doctors usually treat rickettsia with antibiotics for a week.
A zurna is a loud wind instrument from Turkey and the Balkans.
The zurna and drum played at the wedding.
You can hear the zurna from far away.
He learned to play the zurna from his grandfather.
Thiocyanate is a chemical used in labs and industry.
The solution turned red when we added thiocyanate.
Smokers have more thiocyanate in their blood.
The teacher showed us a test with iron and thiocyanate.
A chemoreceptor is a cell that senses chemicals.
Taste buds have chemoreceptors that sense sweet and salty.
Chemoreceptors in the nose help us smell.
Blood chemoreceptors notice when oxygen is low.
A discussant comments on a paper at a conference.
The discussant asked the speaker three good questions.
I am the discussant for the second panel.
Each paper will have a discussant who responds to it.
Eidos is a Greek word for form or idea in philosophy.
Plato used eidos to mean the perfect form of a thing.
The lecture explained eidos in simple terms.
For Aristotle, the eidos of a thing is its form.
Play this part andante, not too fast.
The second movement should be played andante.
The choir sang the hymn andante.
The music teacher wrote "andante" above the first line.
A hydroperoxide is a compound with an oxygen-oxygen-hydrogen group.
Old cooking oil can form hydroperoxides.
Hydroperoxides can be dangerous and may explode.
The lab tested the solvent for hydroperoxides.
Backtracking is a way of solving problems by trying and undoing steps.
The sudoku program uses backtracking to find the answer.
Backtracking can be slow for big problems.
We wrote a backtracking algorithm in class today.
Trachyte is a light gray volcanic rock.
The old streets are paved with trachyte.
Trachyte is used as building stone in Italy.
The geologist found trachyte near the old volcano.
An ionomer is a plastic with charged groups inside.
Golf ball covers are often made from ionomer.
The dentist used an ionomer to fill the tooth.
Ionomer films are used in food packaging.
A hartal is a general strike where shops close.
The opposition called a hartal for Monday.
All the shops were closed during the hartal.
Buses did not run because of the hartal.
A festoon is a chain of flowers or lights hung in a curve.
We hung festoons of lights in the garden.
The hall was decorated with paper festoons.
A festoon of flowers hung over the door.
A chromatophore is a cell that holds color in an animal's skin.
Octopuses change color quickly using chromatophores in their skin.
Chromatophores help fish hide from danger.
Under a microscope, you can see the chromatophores open and close.
A corso is a parade of decorated floats or flowers.
The flower corso goes through the town every August.
Thousands of people watched the corso.
Our school made a float for the corso.
Sodium bisulfite is used to keep food and wine fresh.
Some dried fruit contains bisulfite to keep its color.
People with asthma may react to bisulfite.
Add a little bisulfite to clean the brewing equipment.
Dichloromethane is a liquid used to remove paint.
Use dichloromethane only in a room with fresh air.
Dichloromethane was once used to take caffeine out of coffee.
The lab keeps dichloromethane in a special cabinet.
Eugenol gives cloves their strong smell.
Dentists use eugenol to calm tooth pain.
Clove oil from the pharmacy is mostly eugenol.
The dentist put a small eugenol filling in my tooth.
Evolutionism is the belief in evolution as the explanation of life.
The debate was about evolutionism and religion.
The book criticizes social evolutionism in old anthropology.
Early evolutionism said all cultures develop in the same steps.
Experimentalism means trying new and unusual methods in art.
The band is known for its experimentalism.
Her experimentalism made the film hard to understand.
The festival celebrates experimentalism in music.
Incrementalism means making changes in small steps.
The new mayor prefers incrementalism to big reforms.
Critics say incrementalism is too slow.
Incrementalism helped the company improve year by year.
A laryngoscope is a tool to look at the voice box.
The doctor used a laryngoscope to check my throat.
Nurses prepared the laryngoscope before surgery.
The laryngoscope has a small light at the end.
Limonite is a brown mineral made of iron.
Limonite gives some soil its brown color.
People once made iron from limonite.
We found limonite in the old mine.
Maltodextrin is a white powder added to many foods.
This sports drink contains maltodextrin for quick energy.
Check the label for maltodextrin if you watch your sugar.
Food companies add maltodextrin to make sauces thicker.
Neocolonialism is control of poor countries through money and trade.
The speaker accused rich nations of neocolonialism.
Some people see big foreign loans as neocolonialism.
Our class discussed neocolonialism in Africa.
Nifedipine is a medicine for high blood pressure.
The doctor prescribed nifedipine for my chest pain.
Nifedipine can cause headaches at first.
Do not drink grapefruit juice with nifedipine.
Propanol is an alcohol used in cleaning products.
Hand sanitizer often contains propanol to kill germs.
Clean the screen with a little propanol.
Propanol dries very quickly and leaves no marks.
Spiritism is the belief that we can talk with the dead.
Spiritism became popular in the nineteenth century.
Her grandmother practiced spiritism and held meetings at home.
Many people in Brazil follow spiritism.
Tetrahydrofuran is a liquid used to dissolve plastics.
Tetrahydrofuran is often called THF in the lab.
Keep tetrahydrofuran away from flames because it burns easily.
This plastic pipe glue contains tetrahydrofuran.
Transvestism means wearing clothes of the opposite sex.
The documentary is about the history of transvestism.
Today most people say cross-dressing instead of transvestism.
The book talks about transvestism in old theater.
transvestism.note: This word is dated; "cross-dressing" is more common today.

ex: A wapiti is a large North American deer, also called an elk.
We saw a wapiti near the road in the national park.
Male wapiti have huge antlers in the fall.
In the fall, you can hear the wapiti calling.
A perceptron is a simple model of a brain cell for computers.
We built a perceptron in our machine learning class.
A perceptron can learn to sort data into two groups.
The perceptron was invented in the 1950s.
In "if A, then B," B is the consequent.
The consequent is the second part of an if-then statement.
Check whether the consequent is true.
Name the consequent in this sentence.
Deadweight is how much weight a ship can carry.
The ship has a deadweight of fifty thousand tons.
Cargo, fuel, and water all count toward deadweight.
Larger tankers have a higher deadweight.
A pouf is a soft round seat with no back.
Put your feet up on the pouf.
We bought a leather pouf for the living room.
The kids sit on poufs to watch TV.
Telecasting means broadcasting a program on television.
The station started telecasting in 1955.
Telecasting of the match begins at eight.
She works in sports telecasting for a local station.
A transversal is a line that crosses two other lines.
Draw a transversal through the parallel lines.
The transversal makes eight angles with the two lines.
Use the transversal to find the missing angle.
A phosphonate is a chemical used in cleaners and weed killers.
This dishwasher powder contains phosphonates to stop spots.
Some medicines for weak bones are phosphonates.
Phosphonates stop scale from forming in pipes.
A femboy is a young man who dresses in a feminine way.
He calls himself a femboy and loves skirts.
The femboy style is popular online.
Some femboys post fashion videos on social media.
Consonance means notes that sound pleasant together.
The chord has a sweet consonance.
The music moves from tension to consonance.
Our teacher explained consonance and dissonance.
The Paleogene period began after the dinosaurs died out.
Many mammals grew larger in the Paleogene period.
These Paleogene fossils are over thirty million years old.
The museum has a room of Paleogene animals.
A triumvir was one of three men ruling together in Rome.
Caesar was a triumvir with Pompey and Crassus.
Each triumvir wanted more power than the other two.
The triumvirs divided the empire between them.
Cytokinin is a plant hormone that helps cells divide.
Gardeners use cytokinin to grow new shoots.
Cytokinins keep leaves green longer after picking.
The lab added cytokinin to the plant cells.
Duralumin is a light and strong aluminum alloy.
Old airplanes were built from duralumin.
This ladder is made of duralumin.
Duralumin is lighter than steel but still strong.
A kapellmeister is the leader of an orchestra or choir.
Bach worked as a kapellmeister for a prince.
The kapellmeister chose the music for the concert.
He became kapellmeister of the city theater.
Provincialism means having narrow, small-town views.
The writer criticized the provincialism of his hometown.
Travel can help you lose your provincialism.
The newspaper was accused of provincialism.
A stereoscope shows two photos as one 3D picture.
Look into the stereoscope to see the picture in 3D.
My grandfather had an old wooden stereoscope.
The museum lets visitors try a stereoscope.
A supercollider is a huge machine that smashes particles.
The supercollider is buried deep underground.
Scientists use the supercollider to study tiny particles.
Building a supercollider costs billions of dollars.
A tetroxide is a compound with four oxygen atoms.
Nitrogen tetroxide is used in rocket fuel.
Osmium tetroxide is very toxic, so wear a mask.
The lab keeps the tetroxide in a sealed bottle.
A thermocline is a layer where water gets cold quickly.
Divers felt the cold when they passed the thermocline.
Fish often stay near the thermocline in summer.
The lake has a thermocline about ten meters down.
A radiosonde is a weather device carried by a balloon.
The weather service launches radiosondes twice a day.
A radiosonde measures temperature and wind high in the sky.
We found a fallen radiosonde in a field.
The guarani is the money used in Paraguay.
Lunch cost about thirty thousand guaranis.
Change your money into guaranis at the bank.
Prices in Paraguay are shown in guaranis.
The Greeks saw the kosmos as an ordered whole.
The book explains the ancient idea of kosmos.
For Pythagoras, numbers ruled the kosmos.
The word kosmos means order in Greek.
A skald was a poet in old Scandinavia.
The skald sang about the king's battles.
Vikings respected a good skald as much as a warrior.
We read a poem by a famous Icelandic skald.
The inti was the money of Peru in the 1980s.
The inti lost its value very fast.
My father kept an old inti note.
Peru replaced the inti with the sol in 1991.
A geotextile is a fabric used in the ground to hold soil.
Put geotextile under the gravel path.
Geotextiles help stop soil from washing away.
The builders laid geotextile before the new road.
A metalloid is an element between a metal and a nonmetal.
Silicon is a metalloid used in computer chips.
Find the metalloids on the periodic table.
Metalloids conduct electricity a little, but not like metals.
We climbed a via ferrata in the Alps.
A via ferrata has steel cables and ladders on the rock.
Wear a helmet on the ferrata.
This ferrata is easy enough for beginners.
ferrata.note: Usually used as "via ferrata" (plural "via ferratas" or "vie ferrate").

ex: An antineutrino is the antiparticle of a neutrino.
Nuclear reactors give off many antineutrinos.
Scientists built a detector to catch antineutrinos.
An antineutrino has almost no mass.
A purgative is a strong medicine that empties the bowels.
The doctor gave her a purgative before the test.
Castor oil was an old purgative.
Do not use purgatives too often.
A prospekt is a wide main street in a Russian or Ukrainian city.
Our hotel is on the main prospekt.
Walk down the prospekt to find the shops.
The parade went along the prospekt.
A saccharide is a sugar molecule.
Glucose is a simple saccharide that gives us energy.
Starch is made of many saccharides.
Food labels do not usually say saccharide.
A milliwatt is one thousandth of a watt.
This laser pointer is five milliwatts.
The sensor uses only a few milliwatts.
Lasers over five milliwatts can hurt your eyes.
A dragline is a huge digging machine used in mines.
The dragline moves tons of earth in one bucket.
The mine bought a new dragline.
A dragline can be as tall as a building.
A gateman opens and watches a gate.
The gateman checked our tickets at the entrance.
Ask the gateman to open the gate.
The gateman works the night shift at the factory.
Adiponectin is a hormone made by fat cells.
Low adiponectin is linked to diabetes.
Exercise can raise your adiponectin levels.
The blood test measured adiponectin and other hormones.
Asphodel is a plant with white or yellow flowers.
Asphodel grows wild on Greek hills.
In Greek myths, the dead walk in fields of asphodel.
We saw asphodel flowers on our spring hike.
Betamethasone is a steroid cream for skin rashes.
Put a thin layer of betamethasone on the rash.
The doctor gave her betamethasone injections.
Do not use betamethasone cream for too long.
A caesura is a pause in the middle of a line of poetry.
There is a caesura after the third word.
Mark the caesura with two lines.
The caesura makes the line sound dramatic.
Gastrin is a hormone that makes the stomach produce acid.
Eating a big meal releases gastrin in the stomach.
High gastrin levels can cause ulcers.
The doctor checked his gastrin level.
In Greek myths, ichor is the golden blood of the gods.
The god bled ichor instead of red blood.
The poem describes ichor flowing from the wound.
In the stories, ichor made the gods immortal.
Inosine is a natural substance found in cells.
Some athletes take inosine as a supplement.
Inosine is part of some RNA molecules.
The study tested inosine on brain health.
Monetarism says controlling money supply controls inflation.
Monetarism was popular in the 1980s.
The economist is a supporter of monetarism.
Critics say monetarism caused high unemployment.
Nitromethane is a fuel used in drag racing.
Model cars run on a fuel with nitromethane.
Nitromethane is dangerous and can explode.
The drag racing car burned nitromethane as fuel.
An ordonnance was a royal order in old France.
The king issued an ordonnance on taxes.
The ordonnance created a new army.
Historians studied the old ordonnance in the archives.
